research_mode: official ONS and Home Office sources only; current YE March 2026 crime and outcomes measurements with explicit survey, recording, cohort-maturity and transition limitations; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Robbery split
verified_claims: robbery of personal property fell by 9% to 57,693
overall robbery rose by 10% to 87,362
limitations: overall growth was affected by recording clarification for business robbery

sources.name: Business robbery recording clarification
verified_claims: business-property robbery rose by 91% to 29,669
an April 2025 counting-rules clarification contributed to the increase
limitations: the increase should not be treated as a pure change in underlying offending

sources.name: Shoplifting count
verified_claims: shoplifting fell by 4% to 507,086 offences
the previous-year figure was 530,324
limitations: reporting remains low and recording changes can affect the series

sources.name: CSEW exclusions
verified_claims: the survey excludes businesses, tourists and people in communal establishments
it excludes crimes without a specific victim such as drug possession
limitations: CSEW is not a complete count of all crime

sources.name: Domestic abuse and stalking deferred release
verified_claims: year-ending March 2026 domestic abuse and stalking estimates will be released later
additional quality assurance and analysis are being completed
limitations: the missing estimates must not be inferred from police records

sources.name: Report Fraud launch
verified_claims: Report Fraud launched on 4 December 2025
it replaced Action Fraud and the National Fraud Intelligence Bureau system
limitations: system transition creates a discontinuity in recorded fraud supply

sources.name: Recorded fraud supply suspension
verified_claims: City of London Police may temporarily suspend recorded fraud and cybercrime data supply
the pause supports alignment of legacy and new-system data
limitations: absence from the bulletin is a transition issue, not evidence of zero crime

sources.name: CSEW fraud continuity
verified_claims: CSEW fraud and computer-misuse estimates are unaffected by the police-system transition
limitations: survey and administrative series remain methodologically distinct

sources.name: Police recorded crime 5.2 million
verified_claims: police recorded about 5.2 million crimes excluding fraud and computer misuse
this was 1% lower than 5.3 million
limitations: the count covers reported and recorded notifiable offences only

sources.name: Headline crime reporting rate
verified_claims: an estimated 36% of comparable headline incidents excluding fraud and computer misuse were reported to police
limitations: the percentage is survey-derived and varies by offence type

sources.name: Homicide rate
verified_claims: the homicide rate was 8.1 per million
it fell from 8.9 per million
this was the lowest rate since 2003
limitations: small counts and notable incidents can affect annual rates

sources.name: Knife NDQIS coverage
verified_claims: 41 police forces had switched to NDQIS by March 2026
limitations: method adoption affects comparability with earlier knife series

sources.name: Knife-enabled force shares
verified_claims: Metropolitan Police recorded 28% of knife-enabled offences
West Midlands recorded 8%
Greater Manchester recorded 6%
limitations: force shares are not population-adjusted risk rates

sources.name: Sharp-object hospital admissions
verified_claims: provisional admissions for assault by a sharp object fell by 5% to 3,337
the previous-year figure was 3,523
limitations: hospital admissions measure serious injury demand, not all knife crime

sources.name: Firearm type shares
verified_claims: 38% of firearms offences involved imitation firearms
31% involved handguns
limitations: weapon-type shares apply to the official firearms collection and exclude specified categories
